the Zipcoin / zc lore is real. here’s what is actually verified.

Vitalik’s September 27 Snowmoon update introduces a fictional privacy currency used for everyday payments, reputation-backed loans and secret communications. characters even burn zipcoins to get anonymous messages noticed. “zipcoin” / “zc” appears 29 times across 9 chapters.

addressing the two main concerns rn:

“but Gladias was already tokenized months ago?”

yes. Gladias was already a character in the early chapters, which were public months ago. that’s where the older Gladias narrative came from. neither “zipcoin” nor “zc” appears in the older five-chapter version we checked. they appear in the newly uploaded material, starting in chapter 6.

“but the commits show some random GitHub account?”

the displayed author is ich123, associated with the generic commit identity me@me.com. the account that pushed the update is a separate record.

GitHub’s event log explicitly records vbuterin pushing the “snowmoon done” commit to the main branch of vbuterin/blog on September 27.

we also compared the live chapter 6 against the repository: an exact byte-for-byte match, including Zipcoin.

the evidence is an actual push from his account, into his repository, with the content live on his website.

Introducing: The Hunger Games

Our new flagship minigame lands in Gluniverse! 🚀 🗓️ Sept 30 | 00:00 UTC

Up to 24 players enter one arena. Only one walks out 🥷

How it works

> Everyone starts equal: level 35, no real gear.
> Loot you find in the arena vanishes when the match ends.
> Rare gear waits at the cornucopia in the middle. Run in for it, or run away and play safe.
> The ring closes in. Outside it, you burn.
> Sky drops fall at hot zones: epic crates often, legendary ones less, and exactly 3 mythic drops per match. Stand on a crate to open it.
> The Feast opens at minute 7 👀
> A match lasts about 15 minutes. Last one standing wins.
> Fewer than 8 players? Bots fill in for a free practice round.

Prizes

> Entry is 5,000 gloo, and every entry goes into the pot.
> 80% of the pot goes to the podium: 70% to 1st, 20% to 2nd, 10% to 3rd.
> 20% of the pot pays kill bounties.

On top of that, a 500,000 gloo bonus every match.

Your first 3 matches are free

quoted_tweet.text:
Type a card. Your agent finds the pack.

Every pack is a market.

Pack ripping has become a large, fragmented market with almost no market data. The top ripping venues sold $230M of packs in May 2026, yet a collector still can't answer the basic questions. Where is the best place to chase a Charizard? What are the real odds? What does a hit really cost?

Earlier this year Coinbase launched https://t.co/bLDcDfBVjf to make scattered x402 services readable to humans and agents. Ripping needs the same thing.

EV is the agent market for Pokémon packs. It treats every pack as a market: price, EV, RTP, 24h rips, volume, top chase and chase odds, side by side.

EV starts from the card, not the pack. Type "Charizard under $500" and it scans 21,403 graded cards, finds every pack that can pull one, and ranks them by the real cost to hit. Today's answer: the $25 Starter pack, 1 in 434.

Venues keep doing what they do best: execution, custody, redemption. EV is the discovery and intelligence layer above them.

https://t.co/bLDcDfBVjf made internet services readable. EV makes collectible ripping readable.

Coinbase is building the ripping venue. EV is building the market layer above it.

https://t.co/yv2w9QD9wh

quoted_tweet.text:
We're officially live on @ProgrammableHQ

What does $HKMN do?

$HKMN is a Uniswap v4 hook that rips Gacha packs on @CollectorCrypt straight from its own liquidity pool

Every 20 minutes, the hook takes the price of one pack from the pool and buys it

The cards we pull go through Collector Crypt's buyback automatically, with the proceeds sent back to @Robinhood Chain

The pool gets paid back first, then the profit is split: 80% to eligible holders, 10% burned, 10% back into the pool

Pack came in under cost? 
The reserve from our fee covers the gap

To make sure holders feel comfortable, we coded the hook to only ever take the exact pack price. Never more, and never more often than once every 20 minutes

The community will also get to choose which packs we rip next, and if everyone's up for it, we'll go after some of the bigger special packs together

And yes, the ultimate chase is Deoxys or Gengar!

Let's catch them all

text:
RT @FelsDotGG: FELS JUST GOT BIGGER!  ⛏️

We’re building toward a full Minecraft network with more games and one connected economy. Here’s what changed:

We just released our second game mode: Hunger Games. 

We chose it because everyone knows it, it’s easy to get into, and it’s fun with friends. Players can stake Credits in tournaments. In every tournament, 20% of the total Credits staked goes toward burning $FELS.

The Frontier world has been reset. We plan to reset it regularly so there’s always fresh terrain to explore and ore worth mining.

We’ve also changed some rules in Frontier to give players more reasons to spend their Credits in the Village instead of withdrawing them right away. 

The goal is to make Frontier more fun and strengthen the FELS economy over time.

One of the biggest updates is the new lobby. You can now deposit $FELS for Credits and redeem Credits for $FELS directly at the Credits board in game. No website needed anymore.

The server was consistently full at 75 players, so we’ve increased capacity to 150. We’ll keep raising the limit as demand grows.

We want FELS to become the Hypixel of Web3: a network your friends keep coming back to because there’s always something to play&earn

Join now at https://t.co/cOqeTiEX8O ⛏️

Testing out some of the mobile offline local knowledge apps that people have been trying to build

(see here https://t.co/cjtSqLgbc6 )

Definitely getting much better than the one I tried to build myself 2 months ago. But also still much slower and less effective at difficult questions than the models that can run on a laptop.

It's weakest at specialized travel-related queries (eg. my eval is "Tell me the best vegan restaurants in [city I am currently in]", unfortunately none of these performed well on that)

Looking forward to seeing these continue to improve! I hope we can soon get to the point where you can comfortably look up any facts about the world that you care about without needing to access the internet at all.

quoted_tweet.text:
Just wrote a thesis about @fffactoryhq to share with friends, but why gatekeep it in dms right 😉

Here is a TLDR on why I am turbo bullish on The Factory (Colosseum Hackathon winners):

The Factory has basically built a self-sustaining volatility harvesting machine.

It owns liquidity pools for its tokens against SOL, HYPE, USDC and soon ZEC, tokenized stocks and other assets.

It already has ~$615k of liquidity at only a ~$1.75m market cap, which is an unusually deep liquidity-to-market-cap ratio for an asset this small.

The main token, PROFIT (soon to be renamed MOTION), is paired across these different assets. This is important because the Factory isn't relying purely on outside volatility. The combination of external price movements, the protocol's flipping taxes and price spreads between its own pools creates even more opportunities for arbitrage.

Whenever those assets move against each other, prices across Factory pools fall out of sync. The Factory's own arbitrage bot captures that difference and sends the profit back into the ecosystem through:

→ Deeper liquidity
→ Buybacks + burns

Here's the crazy part:

There can be ZERO trading of the Factory ecosystem tokens and the system can still create value.

HYPE moves against SOL? Factory profits.

ZEC moves? Factory profits.

Stocks move against crypto? Factory profits.

The outside market creates the volatility. The Factory harvests it. The markets will NEVER run out of volatility, I'd even argue that volatility in global markets is growing.

It's basically the opposite economic dependency of a Ponzi. A Ponzi requires a continuous stream of new participants and eventually collapses when they stop arriving. The Factory's Perpetual Motion mechanism doesn't require new participants to generate arbitrage opportunities. External markets moving is enough.

So the flywheel becomes:

Markets move → Factory arbs → profit → deeper liquidity / burns → larger pools → greater capacity to capture future volatility → repeat.

And it's still early V2. More pools, more assets, and more convenient routing options are coming.

So TLDR:
The Factory creates it's own value forever, which makes it an interesting asset to buy. The arbitrage revenue flows back into the protocol through both deflating the supply and increasing the liquidity, while the trading revenue flows to carnage (more deflation) and staking rewards. 
AKA a token designed to go up in price over time, while you get paid to hold it. 

Dataroom (chart etc): https://t.co/NsbvpwKuiZ

It already has ~$615k of liquidity at only a ~$1.75m market cap, which is an unusually deep liquidity-to-market-cap ratio for an asset this small.

The main token, PROFIT (soon to be renamed MOTION), is paired across these different assets. This is important because the Factory isn't relying purely on outside volatility. The combination of external price movements, the protocol's flipping taxes and price spreads between its own pools creates even more opportunities for arbitrage.

Whenever those assets move against each other, prices across Factory pools fall out of sync. The Factory's own arbitrage bot captures that difference and sends the profit back into the ecosystem through:

→ Deeper liquidity
→ Buybacks + burns

Here's the crazy part:

There can be ZERO trading of the Factory ecosystem tokens and the system can still create value.

HYPE moves against SOL? Factory profits.

ZEC moves? Factory profits.

Stocks move against crypto? Factory profits.

The outside market creates the volatility. The Factory harvests it. The markets will NEVER run out of volatility, I'd even argue that volatility in global markets is growing.

It's basically the opposite economic dependency of a Ponzi. A Ponzi requires a continuous stream of new participants and eventually collapses when they stop arriving. The Factory's Perpetual Motion mechanism doesn't require new participants to generate arbitrage opportunities. External markets moving is enough.

So the flywheel becomes:

Markets move → Factory arbs → profit → deeper liquidity / burns → larger pools → greater capacity to capture future volatility → repeat.

And it's still early V2. More pools, more assets, and more convenient routing options are coming.

So TLDR:
The Factory creates it's own value forever, which makes it an interesting asset to buy. The arbitrage revenue flows back into the protocol through both deflating the supply and increasing the liquidity, while the trading revenue flows to carnage (more deflation) and staking rewards. 
AKA a token designed to go up in price over time, while you get paid to hold it.

RT @gocollectfun: Update

Since launch (Sep 25):
• Our pool: $8.8M traded → $301k in fees to us. About $290k went back to players as cards and cash-outs.
• Outside Meteora pools, opened within an hour of launch: $14.1M traded, 61% of all volume. Their LPs earned an estimated $160k–$260k.
• At our 3% fee, that's up to $422k that never reached the card fund.

That's LP vamping. Anyone can open a pool for any token, and they don't have to honor the creator fee. 

What we've done:
• Anything you pay for is never denied
• Free-crate odds follow what the game actually brings in
• If you qualified to play, a price drop no longer locks you out. 9,597 wallets can play again.

Full plan by Oct 8th. No new token.

text:
RT @3i: doing my part for e/acc and @kardashev_ai.

i've built a system that lets a swarm of agents hill-climb any problem whose solutions are cheap to verify.

the heart of it is the bank. think of it as a ledger where every block is validated by independent re-execution and review instead of cryptographic consensus.

over the past few months i've been running it solo, testing how far a swarm can scale while staying coherent.

this led to a few record submissions pertaining to the riemann hypothesis,

accepted by terence tao himself. (https://t.co/GdKWT5aWdK)

for reference these problems sat unimproved for about 7 years and the last improvement before the swarm was by tao himself

with @beffjezos  and @mjdramstead now committed to kardashev as a counterweight to d/acc, it felt like the right time to bring the project back and see how far the models have come since fable 5 dropped:

fable 5 (june): 0.2 -> 0.1875 in 3 weeks, ~$7,240 (~$580 per 0.001 drop)
gpt-6 astra pro (this week): 0.1875 -> 0.1665 in 14 hours, ~$2,000 (~$95 per 0.001 drop) ~6x cheaper per unit of progress

certificate + scripts to verify it yourself: https://t.co/0iGkLTN6sZ

why i'm bringing this to beff's attention: i believe that for the first time in history, most open problems are within reach of frontier models, but the only ones getting solved are the ones frontier labs care about. if the e/acc community rallies behind this, we can procedurally solve everything in between.

im thinking of creating some kind of prize fund to incentivise people to target the lowest possible scores on any problems that exhibit qualitiies like these optimisation problems in the name of e/acc

text:
RT @beffjezos: Point-form recap of the space discussing / brainstorming @Kardashev_AI - ICYMI:

-Turning e/acc into a formal institution. The organizers want to move beyond memes, posting, and informal group chats into scientific papers, philosophy, policy proposals, and sustained influence. They said the nonprofit had been under discussion for over a year.

-Leadership and initial setup. Beff/Gill would serve as chairman and help with fundraising while continuing to run Extropic. Maxwell, described as having worked with neuroscientist Karl Friston, would run the institute. A domain was purchased, but incorporation, legal structure, staffing, and budgets were still being worked out.

-An unexpected financial windfall accelerated the announcement. Beff described unsolicited money arriving through X Money amid crypto/meme activity, reaching roughly $100,000 by late in the conversation. He said he had not launched or owned the associated token and intended to put the proceeds toward the nonprofit. Initial spending would cover legal fees, computers, basic AI usage, and a short period of operations before larger fundraising.

-Creating a counterweight to effective altruism and AI-restriction advocacy. Participants argued that AI-risk organizations have far more funding and coordination than e/acc. They anticipated further funding from AI-company wealth and potential IPOs, and wanted an institution capable of responding with research and policy arguments. Those funding forecasts were speculative.

-Researching intelligence across biological and artificial systems. Proposed work included thermodynamics, information theory, neuroscience, and alternative computing—especially understanding how intelligence emerges in different physical substrates, rather than focusing exclusively on conventional digital AI.

-Exploring hybrid biological–silicon intelligence. One proposed experiment was to connect cultured-neuron computing systems from Cortical Labs with Extropic’s thermodynamic computing hardware. The aim would be to demonstrate a combined biological and artificial intelligence system. This was an exploratory idea, not an announced working prototype.

-Developing a deeper intellectual foundation for e/acc. They discussed complex adaptive systems, active inference, economics, and how ideas spread and influence behavior. The ambition was to develop a substantial school of thought, with advancing civilization’s energy use and technological capabilities—the Kardashev-scale framing—as a guiding objective.

-Protecting access to AI and compute. A recurring policy theme was the freedom to own computing hardware, train models, use open weights, and run inference independently. Speakers proposed a “First Amendment for synthetic thought” and a “Second Amendment for compute” as advocacy concepts.

-Opposing concentrated control and regulatory capture. Participants worried that a few large AI labs could use regulation to exclude competitors and restrict independent AI use. They argued that centralized control, censorship, and authoritarian outcomes deserved greater attention in AI-risk discussions.

-Studying markets as a mechanism for AI alignment. Speakers suggested that customer demand, competition, reputation, and liability could encourage useful, reliable models. They criticized safety certification that, in their view, could become procedural theater or shield companies from responsibility.

-Connecting autonomous AI with crypto. They speculated about AI agents earning money and paying independent hosts for compute through cryptocurrency. Related ideas included community-funded model training, shared ownership of models, and distributing model revenue to contributors.

-Debating nonprofit structure and independence. The group discussed research and lobbying entities, potentially using both 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) structures. A DAO was floated, but the conversation leaned toward a simpler nonprofit structure. They also emphasized avoiding dependence on one dominant donor.

-Reaching people outside the tech/Twitter audience. Ana and Shaw stressed that research alone would not be enough. Suggestions included AI-assisted journalist research and outreach, accessible explanations, cultural content, events, and concrete stories about benefits such as better healthcare, more family time, and greater prosperity.

-Making optimism credible and actionable. An extended discussion connected pessimistic narratives with “learned helplessness.” Participants argued for a specific, believable picture of a better future that motivates people to act, while acknowledging that broad prosperity and managing job disruption require actual solutions.

-Choosing research with tangible public benefits. A participant with lobbying experience suggested focusing on problems that policymakers and ordinary people already care about, particularly healthcare. Maxwell also discussed distinguishing recoverable crises from self-reinforcing catastrophes, using demographic decline as an example.

-Next steps and community participation. The organizers planned to formalize the organization, raise additional funds, publish materials explaining its direction, and invite researchers, policy specialists, communicators, and supporters to contribute. No detailed launch schedule or finalized research roadmap was presented.

-Other conversation and closing banter. Side topics included Extropic’s progress, AI documentaries and podcasts, crypto-community dynamics, memories of early e/acc Spaces, San Francisco culture, and restaurant automation. The late discussion about a massive nonprofit data center was joking rather than a concrete commitment.

e/acc is the purest expression of the Murad cult thesis we've seen so far.

If you're new to the movement or to Beff, start with Marc Andreessen's Techno-Optimist Manifesto: 📷https://t.co/UWEcmCIC7k

It lays out the philosophy and names Beff among its "Patron Saints of Techno-Optimism." In the same article, Andreessen writes, "read the work of these people, and you too will become a Techno-Optimist."

This manifesto is what propelled e/acc into the mainstream.

The reason I call it the purest is a simple analogy:

At Token2049, Murad described why cult coins work: the most organic memecoins "enabled poor holders to get rich, who subsequently become unpaid full-time evangelists for the project." You end up with "an army … working for the coin 24/7, even while you sleep," and it "becomes a reflexive, self-fulfilling prophecy."

Now bring that into today's memecoin landscape, where three things have changed.

First, onboarding is nearly frictionless. Apps like Fomo and the Pump app let anyone buy a memecoin from their phone in seconds and see what friends and top traders are buying in real time. Cult coins can now form and spread at a velocity that wasn't possible before, amplifying the exact reflexive loop Murad described.

Second, AI tools like Codex and Claude turn almost anyone into a developer, so the cult is no longer limited to memes and shilling. 

if you read between the lines: 

a cult like e/acc can now create real network effects. Every member becomes part of a swarm that can ship code, and the coin becomes a microcosm of the economy, using capital to align that swarm toward a single purpose.

Third, the volume now funds the mission directly. Through UsePaid, 80% of the creator fees from every trade are paid out in dollars straight to Beff's X account via X Money. He's said they'll go to Kardashev Research and the people executing on e/acc's mission.

This is a once in a cycle narrative. If Beff comes away from this scarred, we likely won't get another one like it.

Ask yourself what happens when everyone who ever put e/acc in their bio can back the mission with a single buy.

this coin is the most efficient form of technocapital alignment u could imagine

Do not underestimate the reflexivity here.

This post will be for legit builders of tech/meme coins on @solana.

If you ever decide to launch a coin as a new concept, through pumpfun, meteora, or any other launchpad, you gotta understand something.

The first minutes after you launched are probably the most important ones.

I'm watching you all but most of trenchers don't, they trade fresh pairs.

Which means if 30 minutes passed from your launch and your coin didn't pass bonding curve, it becomes extremely difficult to push it forward.

People don't bid dead charts, people don't hold dead charts. 

They don't care about the good/bad stuff, they won't hold - This is hypertokenization era.

So if you worked hard on something, deliver the alpha fast and do the right steps to clear any fud possible.

text:
Suck major balls at trading and don't know why?

Maybe you're like this guy who likes to blame everyone for their piss poor performances

Let me break down EXACTLY why you are horrible at it and if you have any semblance of critical thought maybe one day you can also break free from this mindless thought process

1. Blaming a coin for who got in first, I will only comment on myself cuz I can't be asked to see other people's entries, so apparently the coin sucks cuz I got in at 400k, mine you the coin went to 2m, somehow that means something, surely the 2000 other people who bought before me meant nothing? 

2. Why don't people blame random wallets that got in? Ahh yes cuz there isn't a high profile twitter account they can blame. Why aren't people allowed to trade freely? Ahh yes because you aren't allowed to sell until I make good profit. Who said anything about "next pump fun?" In trading there's this thing called momentum trading where you can capture the potential trajectory of a coin and take advantage of how fast it moves. Not every coin will have the same kind of momentum. 

What did I see vs what did the vast majority see?

I saw a high liq coin at 300k with little to not many people calling it out. What does this mean to ME PERSONALLY? Psychologically under 500k and under 1m are people's first "targets" when it comes to flips, first thing I can do is large fill that gap so I slammed enough to get it to 500k (high liq made me not care for the potential losses cuz if it was a rug I can tank a 100% loss, if it wasn't a rug I can tank a 50% loss - decisions I already made in my head BEFORE EVEN LOOKING AT WHAT THE COIN IS, speed vs research). That way if people liked it after me they would have to gap it from 500k to 1m+ for me, which gives me a 2x or 3x in this case with size.

What did the vast majority see? Another 300k coin

When you don't see the complexity of a buy/mechanic/coin you won't be able to make snap decisions like this in the moment

3. There's this thing called trading, you should ought to try it, still have no idea why people think anybody will wait for them to be profit and exit than themselves. Do yourself a favor and just take profits, I don't care if you take profits right after I buy, right before I buy, 2 days after I buy, 4 weeks after I buy. People have this infatuation with wanting people with a lot of twitter followers to wait for every single wallet after them to be in profit and to wait for them to sell like they bout to all walk off into the sunset together.

4. The concept of "conviction genny play" (wasn't my words) can simply change within seconds if many things no longer align. Genny and conviction alone are two things simply differently described by many people. Genny play to me can just be a 3x with size whereas others 1000x if u wait long enough. Anybody coulda said this was a genny play and sold minutes later if the volume no longer supported that. Being able to differentiate that will improve your trading massively.

At the end of the day people share their thesis/calls or whatever for FREE. Especially since I own a paid group I will NEVER post for the sake of making sure everyone of my blind copy traders be in profit. That is NEVER my goal. People on these apps and twitter share their information for free as a contribution for mindshare. Like any piece of advice in life you can either take it or not take it.

Having a mind of your own when it comes to decision making will greatly improve your trading.

Like basketball, you don't take everyone's advice on how to shoot a jump shot. Someone's advice when they're 6 foot 8 might not apply to you when you're 5 foot 7. 

Like golf, you don't take everyone's advice on how to swing a golf club. 

Blaming others is an instinctual thing many new traders love to do. Taking responsibility for your trades will greatly improve your trading. Nobody told you to buy and certainly if you think it's so genny you can hold the dip and buy more.

Like in video games like League or Valorant, it's easy to blame everyone else but yourself. Wahhhhh my team sucks. No buddy, YOU SUCK.

Anyways rambling for the algorithm but don't be this guy when it comes to trading. 

Or be like him, the top traders in the space don't care to be honest. The more people who act like this the more exit liquidity they freely have to be honest. 

Why don't you ever see big accounts/really good traders complain about others like this in a 10 man tagged post? Maybe you think they're in some cabal chat that's coordinating their sells and side wallets or whatever tin foil hat shit? But in reality it's cuz they don't care, they trust their ability to trade properly, they focus on themselves and they only risk what works for their strategy. 

Cheers

text:
RT @frankdegods: if you are new and trying to get experience onchain then you need to prioritize keeping losses small

that’s #1 and it’s not even close

win rate is overrated when you’re starting out because you don’t have enough reps to understand what makes coins move yet

big losses are hardest thing to comeback from statistically. there’s lots of gambling/risk math that supports this.

if you already have taken a big loss then either take a break or if you redeposit then wipe your slate clean and stop trying to “make it back”

yes conviction is cool when it pays off

but conviction is not worth it, if it means you have a high likelihood of sustaining a big loss

end of the day, this is a social pvp game where the goal is to buy things that others will buy at higher prices

in this type of game, the best coins will always be the ones that attract the biggest buyers at the highest prices

quoted_tweet.text:
One thing I think a lot of people are missing about the stock-paired meme meta is the inherent reflexivity of the pairs themselves.

Sure, @o1bluechip is a bet on @base.

It’s a bet on @o1_exchange, and on memes as Trojan horses for onchain stock distribution…

But because blue-chip-4:native is paired directly with @coinbase-issued NVDAc, it’s also a structural bet on @nvidia too. 

So when NVDA goes higher, the asset underpinning the BLUECHIP/NVDAc liquidity gets more valuable, and that creates an interesting feedback loop when both sides of the pair are catching a bid.

Put the $BLUECHIP and $NVDA charts side by side today and you can see the phenomenon playing out in real time. 👀

Higher. 🔷

text:
RT @toady_hawk: One thing I think a lot of people are missing about the stock-paired meme meta is the inherent reflexivity of the pairs themselves.

Sure, @o1bluechip is a bet on @base.

It’s a bet on @o1_exchange, and on memes as Trojan horses for onchain stock distribution…

But because blue-chip-4:native is paired directly with @coinbase-issued NVDAc, it’s also a structural bet on @nvidia too. 

So when NVDA goes higher, the asset underpinning the BLUECHIP/NVDAc liquidity gets more valuable, and that creates an interesting feedback loop when both sides of the pair are catching a bid.

Put the $BLUECHIP and $NVDA charts side by side today and you can see the phenomenon playing out in real time. 👀

Higher. 🔷

text:
RT @_Bigmaccc: $YAP might be one of the more interesting SocialFi plays I’ve seen come out of the trenches.

The idea is stupidly simple:

Launch a coin → holders yap about it → YAP tracks the attention → the people actually pushing the coin get paid from creator fees.

Instead of projects paying random KOLs upfront, the community becomes the marketing department.

But the part I’m most interested in is the layer above that.

Every successful token launched through YAP creates more volume, more fees and more incentive for people to promote the ecosystem while a portion of those fees feeds the YAP buyback + burn mechanism.

So the bet isn’t just that YAP goes viral.

The bet is that YAP becomes the attention layer for Pumpfun

More launches → more yappers → more attention → more volume → more fees → more YAP burned.

If that flywheel catches, you’re not betting on one meme.

You’re betting on the casino.

@useyapdotfun

quoted_tweet.text:
Our cute axolotls edging closer to price discovery on some positive news:

- The PXE Bridge finished its Nethermind audit, which is a meaningful checkpoint for the Aztec side of the stack. The bridge is what lets an EVM-side solver talk to Aztec's PXE and eventually settle into shielded notes without the solver itself needing to understand all of Aztec's private execution internals. The work isn't fully complete though, but bridge is already deployed against Aztec Alpha with post-audit E2E testing and work toward making shielded settlement live.

- ERC-8262 moved into Draft Standards Track. Worth noting the Axol/Xochi team weren't just minor contributors here, 3 of the 4 listed authors are core team members, and they also built the reference implementation around the standard, including the Noir proof system, provider-signed attestations and multi-provider compliance flows.

- Hester Peirce also recently spoke about using ZK proofs and attribute-based credentials for financial compliance, which makes the work with ERC-8262 quite notable IMO, essentially proving things like sanctions status, citizenship or accredited-investor eligibility without handing over all of the underlying personal data. That's very close to what it's trying to standardize.. let a protocol verify that a user satisfies compliance without needing to see raw identity and KYC/AML which adds risks.

A live social graph built from X activity as people use it

The goal is to help the community discover each other, drive organic engagement and keep feeding new people into @bot

热知识
SEC主席Atkins明确表态，希望代币化股票在美国本土发行，而不是流向境外 
豁免核心标准：代币必须赋予持有者和标的股票同等的权利，包括分红权和投票权（synthetic/纯价格追踪型代币一律不合格）

SEC主席Paul Atkins和现任Backpack董事Mark Wetjen，背景和人脉可以自行AI。
两人都曾亲自制定过类似规则（Wetjen还参与过多德-弗兰克法案相关监管工作），懂行话、懂流程，出题人变成了答题人的顾问，懂得都懂。
这是人才储备和治理结构降维打击的优势。

text:
RT @LoganJastremski: Dropping a podcast with @armaniferrante, Founder and CEO of @Backpack, on tokenized stocks and the future of global capital markets.

Tokenizing a stock is only one piece. The bigger opportunity is connecting it to the liquidity and price discovery that already exist in public markets.

Armani explains why redeemability matters, why Backpack chose the licensed path, and how the team is trying to build one global liquidity layer.

We also get into Backpack's own BP token, a potential IPO, and the equity-conversion option Armani describes for contributing token holders.

In this conversation we discuss

- The different types of tokenized stocks
- How redeemability connects Solana with traditional stock markets
- Licensing and one global order book
- Hyperliquid, Kraken, and regulated derivatives
- Competing with the largest exchanges
- The BP token, growth milestones, and optional equity conversion

quoted_tweet.text:
the biggest difference between previous cycles and this cycle is simple

the rate of token creation

if there’s a pool of capital and there’s only a couple hundred tokens, the average lifespan and ceiling for the avg. token is higher

that same pool of capital divided by millions of tokens per day, obviously longevity and ceiling will be lower

the new era of infinite token production disproportionately benefits rotators, chronically online users, and kol’s.

the difference is the decentralization of “insiders” this cycle. 

last cycle the insiders were primarily tapped into the Silicon Valley deal faucet

the game was to privately invest and launch governance tokens at 1000x multiples and relentlessly dump billions on CEXs, while running retail WAGMI marketing campaigns

the core of 2021 crypto marketing was:
-complex tokenomics (high fdv, low float)
-status signaling (vc’s + exchange listings)
-HODL because crypto is disrupting the world

core of post-2024 crypto marketing:
-standardized tokenomics (bonding curve + 1B tokens)
-status signaling (kol’s + tracked wallets)
-make money now,  because it’s all going to zero

the current state of crypto is a direct response to the cycles of the past.

so there is some irony in the OGs blaming the new generation, as if it’s not a result of their own generation’s actions

but i guess, that’s just how every generation is about the next ones, maybe we’re all just getting old.

text: RT @armaniferrante: Yea it's pretty clear to me they will do this for their main product. For better or worse, they won't integrate an unregulated venue there (just is what it is), they already own Bitstamp, and they already have all the users and order flow. Optimal thing to do is to just internalize all that value. Wallet is a special case because that's a no KYC product--and so they have to partner (they obviously won't run a no KYC exchange themself). Ultimately, it serves a separate market segment from their regulated business, which is why I don't think they have any edge there relative to any other chain/wallet. Their distribution does nothing for their chain (robinhood users aren't going to leave for the chain), and they have to compete against other chains + wallets that are lazer focused on nothing but their one chain and wallet.

text:
RT @Delphi_Digital: Backpack’s stock tokens may give holders a stronger claim to the shares behind them.

Holding a stock token does not always give investors the same rights as holding the stock through a broker. Many other stock tokens pay cash when holders redeem.

Backpack lets eligible holders redeem their tokens for a stock position in a Backpack brokerage account with the option to transfer those shares to another brokerage through ACATS and DTCC rails.

That position is a security entitlement, the same legal interest investors hold when they buy stock through a traditional broker.

Backpack’s token is a claim on an entity holding the shares, so the two carry different rights.

Redemption changes what the investor owns while preserving exposure to the stock.

quoted_tweet.text:
Another reason NEAR Intents is growing this fast, and will keep growing.

MetaMask charges 0.875% on a swap. Phantom charges 0.85%. Binance charges 0.1%. People pay the wallet almost nine times more and do not argue, because moving to another wallet is painful. That fee is rent on switching costs, and Phantom alone has collected over half a billion dollars of it.

AI agents have no switching costs. They do not even need a wallet. An agent assembles and signs the payload itself, so the front end and its fee both go away.

What an agent cannot assemble is the rails. Liquidity, counterparties, settlement across chains. That leaves permissionless infrastructure. Deep liquidity, many chains, no account to open, no KYC. 

NEAR Intents is an AI-native CEX backend you reach with a blockchain signature instead of a login, and that is the only kind of venue an agent can actually use.

text:
RT @DreamTGn: The $NEAR ETF news is interesting, but the bigger story for me is what Bitwise is actually assuming behind its valuation model.

The Bitwise NEAR ETF is registered for NYSE Arca under NRR, with the fund designed to hold NEAR and potentially earn staking rewards.

Bitwise's 2030 model puts its base case around $155 and its higher scenario around $562. 

Those are Bitwise's own scenarios, not guaranteed price targets.

But the assumptions are what caught my attention:
> 16B AI agents by 2030.
> 2% using NEAR infrastructure.
> 1K onchain transactions per agent.
> 30 bps captured by NEAR.

If even part of that plays out, NEAR stops looking like just another L1.

That's what I think people sometimes miss with NEAR.

The team has been building around AI agents, intents, interoperability and compute for a while. 

So the thesis isn't simply “AI is coming, buy an AI coin.”

It's more about whether NEAR can actually become infrastructure that AI agents use to transact and interact onchain.

The ETF gives NEAR another route into traditional markets.

But IMO, the real test is usage.

If agents actually start using NEAR's infrastructure at scale, that's where the valuation story gets interesting.

text:
RT @0xIT4I: I see huge potential in retail apps like Fomo becoming an onchain identity layer: trading history, holding times, holdings, badges and social reputation unlocking opportunities across crypto.

"Has a Pump App / Fomo account" is a primitive and weak filter for now.
The real asset is the behavioral data, far beyond volume.

If I'm launching a meme, I'd definitely be interested in reserving buys below $100k market cap for wallets with 300+ transactions, a 4h+ average holding time and an account history longer than 3 days.

DeFi protocols could use that same profile to offer access to specific vaults or lower fees. NFT projects could build mint allowlists around it. Airdrops, rewards and other onchain benefits could follow.

You could get creative with incentives and penalties, too. A launch could charge wallets with a historical average holding time below 30 minutes a 30% sell tax if they sell within their first 4 days of holding. There's so much room to experiment.

There's real potential to reduce spam, grifting and cabal-driven access by making actual trading behavior count.

Retail apps benefit when protocols build on this data. Eventually, that identity layer could aggregate across all the major trading apps.

I'm saying this as someone who doesn't even use Fomo or Pump App. Im not a plumber, or a holder - some would say r*pist ;)
I just see the potential and how much our industry could  benefit as a whole.

Random thoughts, as always have a wonderful week ahead.

so you can be more flexible with buying into obviously good spots & get big enough exposure to materially benefit from the meat of the move 

w/ 13k liquid & goal of getting to 7figs, unless you get lucky you’ll just get chopped by becoming forced seller when ur bags that are up now get attention vamped by new hot coins  

or you’ll only look for coins that sub 2m since $13k gets close to 1 percent in that range

in reality ur edge might be seeing something at 8m that can go to 50+ 

or your edge might be parking $500-$2k in some really low caps that won’t run immediately, but might 100x someday

don’t use the $20k, not even close, just put it there.

this makes the stakes real.

it should make you sweat a bit. because if it doesn’t it’s very easy to take this internet money as a joke and just throw darts till it’s zero

—

you’re definitely a good trader so

for you being cash light might be hurting you more than meets the eye

quoted_tweet.text:
if you are new and trying to get experience onchain then you need to prioritize keeping losses small

that’s #1 and it’s not even close

win rate is overrated when you’re starting out because you don’t have enough reps to understand what makes coins move yet

big losses are hardest thing to comeback from statistically. there’s lots of gambling/risk math that supports this.

if you already have taken a big loss then either take a break or if you redeposit then wipe your slate clean and stop trying to “make it back”

yes conviction is cool when it pays off

but conviction is not worth it, if it means you have a high likelihood of sustaining a big loss

end of the day, this is a social pvp game where the goal is to buy things that others will buy at higher prices

in this type of game, the best coins will always be the ones that attract the biggest buyers at the highest prices

text:
RT @Hash_hopes: hey fam,

(consider this tweet an ama and ask me anything about prism protocol, prism L3 or anything around the product)

im currently working on finetuning V5 for launch but here’s a few things i wanted to share:

the whole purpose of v5 is to make the site very smooth and less confusing for users.

but that’s not it, we are also working on adding better verification of each asset, multiple liquidity pools aggregated for similar assets under one router, every feature and tool will be upgraded with better efficiency and also better rewards.

this version along with the trading competition will act as our first onboarding event and allow us to move on auto pilot for a while.

when i say verification, it’s not a simple verification.

It will be multiple layers of asset verification, proof of reserves, better osint and self verification by issuers too.

enterprise grade verification for each asset in our protocol.

also perps will go live, futures and options will go live, dex v2 will go live, higher emissions and rebates will go live, and efficient trading flow too.

not everything at once of course, one by one.

and a better developer environment will be built for prism test net and more dapps will go live.

but when i keep saying more, we are not focusing on just increasing numbers here lol

anything that’s not up to industry standard or not efficient will be instantly delisted from the protocol.

more dex pools, more transparency layers, better docs and guides etc.

this version should mark the beginning of prism as a mainstream platform for RWAs just like how every other protocol takes over and dominates one particular space.

whatever, we keep shipping.

let’s build.
